ideas.closest_known_work: Glaser group (Missouri S&T): RuBisCO-mimetic carbon capture and release in solution, with fluoroalkylamine pKa depression and KDDE active-site models (NMR plus computation). KIST/Chung-Ang Univ.: 'A CO2 Absorbent Articulated by Imitating the RuBisCO Regulation Site', a Mg2+-chelate amine complex reported at 2.0 mol CO2 per mol complex (conditions not verified). Long group diamine-Mg2(dobpdc) (CO2 insertion into Mg-N). PEI on Mg-Al LDH (Zhao 2025): 3.92 mmol/g at 400 ppm, 3% H2O, 25 C, 20 cycles, attributed to hydroxyl hydrogen bonding, not Mg-carbamate. Min et al. 2018 epoxybutane-PEI. Difference: Mg2+ is used as a tunable dopant to restore a few kJ/mol to oxidation-hardened commercial-type amines, not as the primary site, and aimed at the stability-capacity trade-off.
ideas.cheapest_falsifying_test: ~$2-3k, 6-8 weeks. Prepare epoxybutane-PEI/silica (~0.4 epoxide per N) with 0, 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 mol Mg/kg. Measure uptake at 400 ppm at 25, 40 and 55 C, dry and 50% RH (TGA or breakthrough), and estimate the isosteric heat. Check carbamate C=O shift by DRIFTS. Run an oxidation test of 18 h at 70 C in dry 0.04% CO2/air. Go if 400 ppm uptake at 25 C and 50% RH rises >=0.25 mol/kg, the heat rises by 2-8 kJ/mol, and oxidative loss is <=1.2x the Mg-free epoxide-PEI. Kill if the humid gain is <0.1 mol/kg (hydration screening) or ageing worsens >1.5x.
ideas.computational_test: DFT with an implicit dielectric (eps 5-20) plus 0-6 explicit waters on Mg. Compare the free energy of a Mg2+-carbamate contact pair with the ammonium-carbamate ion pair in a hydroxyalkyl-substituted amine fragment and map ddG versus Mg hydration number. Go if ddG <= -3 kJ/mol survives with >=4 waters. Pass each ddG through the verifier's Langmuir window, as in bio_pass2.py.
ideas.why_different: Instead of choosing between oxidation-resistant and strongly binding amines, it uses a cheap redox-inert cation to put back the ~4 kJ/mol the stabilisation removed. The verifier shows the target is small and has an upper bound.

ideas.title: Bohr-linkage moisture swing: a rigid quaternary-ammonium scaffold that cycles only linked water
ideas.one_line: Treat the moisture swing like haemoglobin's Bohr effect: only a few water molecules are thermodynamically linked to CO2 release. Put quaternary-ammonium sites in a rigid, low-swelling scaffold so that only those waters cycle, cutting drying time and vapour handling 3-6x.
ideas.conventional_core: Quaternary-ammonium anion-exchange resin (carbonate/bicarbonate) in a vapour or vacuum moisture swing, 20%->95% RH at 25 C.
ideas.graft: Wyman linkage in the haemoglobin Bohr effect. O2 affinity is shifted by a small fixed number of linked protons bound at specific groups in a rigid protein, with no bulk protonation or swelling.
ideas.mechanism: Wyman linkage gives dln p50(CO2)/dln a_w = Delta n_w, the waters released per CO2 bound. For a 20%->95% RH swing that raises equilibrium pCO2 100-500x (Wang/Lackner; Flory up to 500x with liquid water), the linked water is only 3.0-4.0 mol/mol (2.8-5.7 for other RH windows). Measured resins cycle 17-24 mol H2O per mol CO2 by vapour (IRA-900; Lively 2025, Wade 2026) and ~244 by liquid wetting (A501, ASU 2025). So only 13-24% (vapour) or 1-2% (liquid) of the cycled water does thermodynamic work; the rest is common-mode swelling water that every cycle must move, and drying limits the cycle (ASU: 30 min of drying before any CO2 binds). In a rigid, hypercrosslinked or hydrophobic-grafted scaffold, the CO2-linked hydration shell of the QA-carbonate pair stays but bulk swelling is suppressed. The graft is the design principle: linked effector sites in a non-swelling matrix. This competes with idea 1 (release reaction-limited); the same particle-size test separates them.
ideas.key_parameters: QA site density >=3 mmol/g. Scaffold >=20% DVB-equivalent hypercrosslinked polystyrene or a hydrophobic grafted support. Target water swing <=8-10 mol/mol (<=4 mmol/g at 1 mmol/g CO2) with CO2 swing >=0.7 mmol/g, 20%->95% RH, 25 C, 400 ppm. Linked water 3-4 mol/mol. No heat input; product ~1-5 kPa CO2. Lifetime unchanged by design (QA chemistry). Resin $10-54/kg.
ideas.quantitative_claims: (1) Minimum linked water 3.0 mol/mol (100x pCO2 swing) to 4.0 (500x) for 20%->95% RH. (2) Measured linked share is 13-17% (IRA-900 VMS, 24 mol/mol), 18-24% (IRA-900 20->50% RH, 17 mol/mol) and 1-2% (A501 liquid, 244 mol/mol). (3) Latent heat moved per tonne (verifier moisture_swing_water_heat), supplied by ambient air or recovered by condensation: 24.0 GJ/t at 24 mol/mol, 6.0 at 6, 4.0 at 4. Water mass falls from 9.8 to 2.5 t per t CO2. (4) If drying time scales with water removed and release is unchanged, cutting 24 to 6 mol/mol shortens the cycle from 5 h to 3.5 h; productivity rises from 0.19 to 0.27 kg/kg/day (verifier productivity at 0.9 mmol/g). If wetting also scales with water, productivity reaches 0.76 kg/kg/day. (5) Vapour flow in VMS falls ~4x, the variable that drives modelled VMS electricity from 1 to 15 MJ/kg. Script: scratchpad/sorbent/bio_pass2b.py (section F).
ideas.closest_known_work: OptiLex map open problem: decouple the 'switching' waters from bulk swelling (target <=50 wt% water at IEC >=3 mmol/g; ASU achieved sub-50 wt% only at lower ion content; PVDF-blended AERs ~0.9 mmol/g). Quaternised graphene (Small 2024; 3.24 mmol/g at 20% RH). LCST hydrogel PDMH (Adv. Mater. 2026). Moisture-swing thermodynamic hydration models (Shi, Lackner et al.). Co-sorption isotherms (Guzzo 2025; Lopez-Marques 2026). Differences: applying Wyman linkage puts a number on the floor (3-4 linked waters) and gives a measurable criterion, linked versus common-mode water, for selecting or designing scaffolds.
ideas.cheapest_falsifying_test: ~$2-4k, 2 months, DVS/TGA. Measure CO2 isotherms (50-2,000 ppm, 25 C) at 20%, 50% and 95% RH, plus water isotherms in carbonate and bicarbonate forms, on 4-5 commercial strong-base resins spanning gel (low DVB), macroporous (IRA-900) and the most highly crosslinked available, plus one lab-quaternised high-DVB chloromethylated resin (design level). Extract linked Delta n_w from dln p50/dln a_w and the common-mode water. Go if any material shows water swing <=10 mol/mol with CO2 swing >=0.7 mmol/g (20%->95% RH). Kill if CO2 swing falls in proportion to water swing across all materials (linked share stuck near ~15%), which would mean bulk swelling is mechanistically required.
ideas.computational_test: Fit a two-state Wyman/MWC linkage model to published CO2-H2O co-sorption isotherms on IRA-900 (Guzzo et al. 2025; Lopez-Marques et al. 2026) to separate linked from common-mode water. Then use MD of QA-carbonate/bicarbonate hydration shells in a swollen versus rigid hypercrosslinked matrix to check whether the linked waters are first-shell waters that a rigid matrix keeps.
ideas.why_different: It converts the moisture swing's water problem into a measurable biophysical quantity (linked versus unlinked water) with a hard floor of 3-4 mol/mol, rather than treating all water uptake as unavoidable.

ideas.title: Zn-polyamine carbonic-anhydrase sites inside humid PEI: make the slow bicarbonate route fit in a fast cycle
ideas.one_line: Dope supported PEI with ~1 mol% Zn(II) per N so that Zn-OH sites, the CA active-site motif, catalyse the humid bicarbonate pathway. Fast cycles could then use whatever bicarbonate capacity humid air offers instead of leaving it to hour-scale chemistry.
ideas.conventional_core: Supported PEI (40-50 wt% on silica or alumina, or laminate) in steam-assisted temperature-vacuum swing, adsorbing humid ambient air in 20-40 min steps.
ideas.graft: Carbonic anhydrase catalysis: a Zn-bound hydroxide with pKa near neutral attacks CO2 directly to give bicarbonate, bypassing slow base catalysis.
ideas.mechanism: In humid amine sorbents, free CO2 binds first as carbamate (fast). Bicarbonate, which can reach 1 CO2 per N, needs CO2 hydration. At 420 ppm the free CO2 is only ~1.4e-5 M, so the hydration flux is tiny. Uncatalysed water/OH- paths need 5-130 h to build 0.25 M bicarbonate in the amine phase. Solution-like tertiary-amine base catalysis (~7 /M/s x 4 M) needs ~10 min, and JACS Au 2025 notes that bicarbonate in immobilised amines forms more slowly than carbamate and is seldom seen by IR except at long times and high water loadings. Zn(II) bound by 3 PEI nitrogens with one water forms Zn-OH sites like Zn-tren or Zn-TPA (measured CA-mimic k 650-730 /M/s). At 0.1-0.3 M Zn in the amine phase this gives 70-210 /s, i.e. 1.4-4 min per 0.25 M. Zn is redox-inert, so unlike Cu and Fe it should not catalyse autoxidation if the salt is Cu/Fe-free. Bicarbonate desorbs readily: the uncatalysed t1/2 is ~45 s at 60 C, so regeneration is unaffected. Key uncertainty: the equilibrium bicarbonate share, which caps the prize. An ideal-solution model gives only 0.01-0.28 mol/kg for effective pKa 9-10.5 and water activity 0.3-0.8. A solid-state NMR study (J. Mater. Chem. A 2024) attributes the humid boost in amine sorbents to swelling, not bicarbonate, while COF-999 and MOF-808-Lys show ~1 mmol/g humid gains claimed as bicarbonate.
ideas.key_parameters: PEI ~23 mmol N/g; Zn/N 0.5-2 mol% (52-209 mmol Zn/kg; ties up 1.5-6% of N), added as a Cu/Fe-free Zn salt of a non-oxidising anion. dH -70 kJ/mol, dS -165 J/mol/K for the carbamate. Adsorption 25 C, 400 ppm, 50% RH, 20-40 min; desorption 100 C, 1 kPa. Measured water swing ~3.6 mol/kg (6 mol/mol at 0.6 mol/kg). Zn salt <$0.15/kg sorbent. Sorbent $20/kg.
ideas.quantitative_claims: (1) Time to form 0.25 M bicarbonate at 420 ppm in the amine phase: water path 7,900 min, OH- (pH 10) 343 min, tertiary-amine base ~10 min, Zn mimic 0.1 M 4.2 min, 0.3 M 1.4 min, CA II 10 uM 0.2 min. (2) Ideal-model equilibrium bicarbonate ceiling is 0.01-0.28 mol/kg sorbent (45 wt% PEI); measured humid gains in frameworks reach ~1 mol/kg. (3) If catalysis raises within-cycle working capacity from 0.60 to 0.70-0.80 mol/kg at a fixed water swing per kg, heat falls from 13.1 to 11.5-10.2 GJ/t and work-equivalent from 3.30 to 2.97-2.72 GJ/t (verifier TVSACycle, inert ratio 0.5, 100 C, 1 kPa). Productivity at 36 cycles/day rises from 0.95 to 1.11-1.27 kg/kg/day; sorbent $/t at $20/kg and 10,000 cycles falls from $76 to $65-57. (4) Zn ties up <=6% of amine N at 2 mol%. Script: scratchpad/sorbent/bio_pass2.py (section B) and bio_pass2b.py.
ideas.closest_known_work: Biomimetics 2019: diethylenetriamine-Zn(II) anchored in MCM-41 as a CA mimic, which captures CO2 in humid ambient air as a Zn-bicarbonate (a stoichiometric site, not a catalyst inside an amine phase). Zn-TPA and Zn-TPA-OH mimics with k 648-731 /M/s (Biomimetics 2019, PMC6963681). Zn-N-C single-atom CA nanozyme (ACS Mater. Au 2025). MFU-4l-OH Zn-OH MOF (Dinca 2018). JACS Au 2025 laminate PEI (bicarbonate slow and rarely detected). J. Mater. Chem. A 2024 NMR (humid boost from swelling). OptiLex pass 1 placed Zn-cyclen in K2CO3 films, a different core. Difference: sub-stoichiometric Zn catalysis inside a commercial-type polyamine to accelerate an existing equilibrium.
ideas.cheapest_falsifying_test: ~$1-2k, TGA plus DRIFTS, 4 weeks. 40 wt% PEI/silica with 0, 0.5 and 1 mol% Zn per N. Measure uptake at 400 ppm, 25 C, 50% RH at 10 min, 30 min and 3 h, plus dry capacity; look for bicarbonate bands (~1360 cm-1) versus carbamate. Ageing check: 18 h at 70 C in dry 0.04% CO2/air. Go if 30-min humid uptake is >=0.1 mol/kg above control, dry capacity is within -5%, and ageing loss is <=1.2x control. Kill if the 30-min gain is <0.05 mol/kg; that result also bounds PEI's accessible bicarbonate share. Kill if Zn accelerates ageing beyond 1.2x.
ideas.computational_test: Extend the ideal speciation model in bio_pass2.py with ion-pair activity corrections (low-dielectric ammonium-bicarbonate pairing). Calibrate against measured dry/humid 400 ppm capacities of PEI/silica, Lewatit and COF-999 to estimate PEI's real equilibrium bicarbonate share. Then use a reaction-diffusion model to predict 30-min uptake with and without catalysis; go only if the predicted gain is >=0.1 mol/kg.
ideas.why_different: It does not add capacity or new sites; it makes an existing humid equilibrium reachable within commercial cycle times. The script bounds the payoff explicitly (0.01-0.28 mol/kg ideal; ~1 mol/kg seen in frameworks), so a negative result also measures PEI's bicarbonate share.
